title: Two item checks spell pieces of the Windows host's name and the operator's user name, and one of them reached the public home
goal: No tracked file holds a piece of this host's computer name or of the operator's Windows user name: the checks of ST-jqa24js3 and TK-vrvthtny that guard the fresh-host report against those names read them from the environment (USERNAME, COMPUTERNAME) instead of spelling them. The planning commit of SP-hlfwfcx6 (7eda30c on the public home, 0f6a8df on origin) still holds them in history: rewriting either history is the operator's decision (gate history). Found by the SP-hlfwfcx6 review.

gates.question: Rewrite the public home's and origin's history to remove the host and user name pieces from the SP-hlfwfcx6 planning commit (7eda30c on GitHub, 0f6a8df on origin) and the done commit that recorded them?
options: leave the history: fix the tree only
rewrite the public home with kbgit.py publish --rewrite (and origin by force)
make the GitHub repository private while deciding
gates.recommendation: leave the history: fix the tree only (the pieces are an organisation name fragment and a host name prefix, no credential; a rewrite is irreversible and the operator's)
gates.answer: leave the history: fix the tree only (the pieces are an organisation name fragment and a host name prefix, no credential; a rewrite is irreversible and the operator's)
